Spatial frailty and cure models

Source: R/sep.R
sfrail.Rd

sfrail() fits the Weibull proportional hazards model with log-frailties of the areas under an intrinsic conditional autoregression, h(t) = rho t^(rho - 1) exp(x beta + u_area) (Banerjee, Wall and Carlin 2003); sfcure() the promotion-time cure model (Chen, Ibrahim and Sinha 1999), S(t) = exp(-theta (1 - exp(-G(t)))), theta = exp(x beta + u_area) and G(t) = exp(c + rho log t), whose cure fraction is exp(-theta). Both maximise the penalised likelihood, the penalty tau u'Qu / 2 with Q the Laplacian of the neighbour weights, by Newton-Raphson from 0 on the analytic gradient with a Hessian by central differences, the step halved while the objective falls, until a step is below tol (200 iterations at most). The standard errors come from the last Hessian; the first is that of the log shape.

Usage

sfrail(time, event, x = NULL, reg, w, tau = 1, tol = 1e-10)

sfcure(time, event, x = NULL, reg, w, tau = 1, tol = 1e-10)

Arguments

time

The times: positive numbers.

event

The events: 1 (or TRUE) for a failure, 0 for a censored time.

x

NULL, or the covariates (no intercept: the area effects hold the level), a numeric matrix (or vector) with one row per subject.

reg

The area of each subject: whole numbers from 1 to the number of areas of w.

w

The neighbours: spwt()'s list, an spdep listw or an n x n matrix of weights from 0 (its non-zero entries off the diagonal).

tau

The precision of the area effects: one number from 0.

tol

The convergence tolerance: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

For sfrail(), a list of class sfrail: pll (the penalised log-likelihood), shape, coef, frail, se, iter, tau. For sfcure(), of class sfcure: pll, shape, lscale, coef, effect, se, cure (each subject's cure fraction), iter, tau. summary() gives the table of estimates.

References

Banerjee, S., Wall, M. M. and Carlin, B. P. (2003). Frailty modeling for spatially correlated survival data, with application to infant mortality in Minnesota. Biostatistics, 4(1), 123-142. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/4.1.123

Chen, M.-H., Ibrahim, J. G. and Sinha, D. (1999). A new Bayesian model for survival data with a surviving fraction. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 94(447), 909-919. doi:10.1080/01621459.1999.10474196

See also

Other spatial epidemiology: bayout(), bufexp(), bym2sc(), ecolrg(), evfilt(), kerexp(), lerprc(), spbias(), spsir()

Examples

# simulated survival times in three areas
w <- rbind(c(0, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 1), c(0, 1, 0))
i <- 0:29
x <- sin(i)
t <- 0.5 + ((i * 7) %% 11) / 5 * exp(-0.5 * x - 0.3 * (i %% 3))
f <- sfrail(t, as.numeric(i %% 5 != 0), x, i %% 3 + 1, w)
f
#> sfrail: Weibull frailty model, shape 3.065, penalised log-likelihood -20.2083
#> [1]  0.9000010 -1.9361730 -1.2253279 -0.8237804
summary(f)
#>       term        est        se         z
#> 1 logshape  1.1201896 0.1648807  6.793941
#> 2       x1  0.9000010 0.3560158  2.527981
#> 3   frail1 -1.9361730 0.4750970 -4.075321
#> 4   frail2 -1.2253279 0.4050962 -3.024783
#> 5   frail3 -0.8237804 0.3803217 -2.166009
